description_ru: В дождливую субботу мальчик учится складывать бумажный кораблик и бежит за ним вдоль реки, где встречает старого рыбака.
text:
Sam is eight years old, and he lives in a small town near a river. On Saturday morning it rains, so he cannot play football with his friends. He sits at the kitchen table and looks at the grey window, feeling bored.

"Why don't you make something?" says his mother. She gives him a sheet of colourful paper. "Do you know how to make a boat?"

"No," says Sam.

"Then I show you. My grandfather taught me when I was your age."

She folds the paper once, twice, three times, and slowly a little boat appears in her hands. It is red and white, with two sharp corners at the front. Sam takes it and turns it around.

"Now you make one," says his mother.

Sam tries four times. The first boat is flat, the second has a big hole, and the third looks like a hat. The fourth is not perfect, but it can stand on the table. He writes his name on the side with a blue pen: SAM.

By the afternoon, the rain stops, and the sun comes out between two clouds. Sam puts on his yellow boots and runs to the river with his boat. The water moves fast today, and it is full of leaves and small branches.

"Let me put you in the water," he says to the boat. "Good luck, Sam."

He kneels on the bank and puts the boat on the river. For a moment it turns round and round, and he is afraid it will sink. Then it finds the middle of the water and starts to sail, quickly and proudly, like a real ship.

"Wait for me!" Sam laughs, and he runs along the bank.

He runs past the old bridge and the cafe with the green door. He runs past a woman with a dog, and past two boys on bicycles, who ask where he is going.

"I follow my boat," he says.

"Can we come?" they ask.

"Yes, but it is my boat. I have to see where it goes."

So the three boys run together beside the river. The boat jumps over small waves and turns around a rock.

After ten minutes, the river becomes wide and slow, and the boys come to a place where the trees are high and the grass is thick. Here, the boat stops. It rests against some flowers near the bank, and an old man in a brown hat sits there with a fishing line in his hand.

"Hello," says the old man. "Is this your boat?"

"Yes," says Sam. His voice is a little small because he is out of breath. "It is my first boat. I made it today."

The old man lifts it out of the water with great care. He turns it over in his big, rough hands. "It is a good boat," he says. "Somebody taught you well."

"My mother showed me."

"And who taught her?"

"Her grandfather."

The old man smiles. "Then it is a very old boat, even if it is wet and new. Sit down, boy. You look tired."

Sam sits next to him. The two other boys sit down too, and for a while nobody talks. The river makes a soft sound, and the sun is warm on their faces. Sam looks at the old man's line in the water.

"Do you catch many fish?" he asks.

"Not today," says the old man. "But I come here for the quiet, not for the fish. Fish are a bonus."

"What is a bonus?"

"A gift you do not expect," says the old man. "Like your boat."

He takes a small piece of paper from his pocket, a bit yellow and old, and gives it to Sam. "Fold this one for me. I want to see your hands work."

Sam folds it carefully, once, twice, three times. This time the boat is better. He gives it to the old man.

"Very good," says the old man. "Now you keep that one for me. Put it in the river next week, from this place. I wait for it here."

"But will it find you?"

"Maybe yes, maybe no. That is the fun of it."

When the sun starts to go down, Sam says goodbye and walks home between his two new friends, with the red boat in his hand. It is wet and a bit soft, but he does not mind.

At home, his mother is making soup. "Where are your boots?" she asks. "And why are your feet so wet?"

"Mum, I have a big story for you," says Sam. "It starts with a boat."

He puts the boat on the window next to the kitchen table to dry. Outside, the evening is clear, and far away, the river is still moving, carrying the leaves and the light to the sea.

Начните с «э» и плавно перейдите в «у»; британский вариант слитный.

questions.question: What does Sam's mother teach him to make?
Who does Sam meet by the river?
questions.answer: An old man who is fishing.

questions.question: What does the old man call a gift you do not expect?
What does the old man ask Sam to do next week?
questions.answer: Put a paper boat in the river from the same place.
